title: Predictable Temporary Files in /tmp
platform_conditions: POSIX sh and bash on Linux/macOS; mktemp is available in GNU coreutils, busybox, and macOS, but the legacy mktemp(3) C-call pattern and /tmp/PID naming persist in older install scripts
security_mechanism: A name built as /tmp/name.$$ is fully predictable: the PID is visible to other processes through /proc or ps, so a local attacker creates the path first — as a symlink pointing at a sensitive file, or as a file they hold open — and the privileged script's subsequent redirection writes through the symlink or into attacker-readable state. The check-then-use idiom ([ -f $f ] before writing) does not close the window: the check and the open are separate system calls and the attacker swaps the path between them. mktemp closes this because it creates the file atomically with O_EXCL on a randomized name and prints only the name it owns.

source_sink_clues.source: Local attacker visibility in multi-user /tmp, shared CI workspaces, and setuid or root-run install scripts whose PID and filename layout are observable.
source_sink_clues.sink: Redirection or writes to /tmp paths built from $$, fixed names, or user-influenced components; mktemp invoked with a template lacking X's or on a path the attacker can pre-create; any [ -f ]/[ -e ] test followed by a separate open/write of the same path in a privileged script

tracking_guards: Check temporary files are created only via mktemp (template with at least three trailing X's) inside a directory the script controls, or via mktemp -d for multi-file work; check no user-influenced component enters the temp path; check privileged scripts never write into a world-writable directory by predictable name and avoid test-then-write idioms.
not_candidate_when: The temporary name comes from mktemp/TEMPDIR created at runtime with O_EXCL semantics, the script writes inside a private directory (0700 runtime dir, mktemp -d) instead of /tmp, or the target system is single-user with no untrusted local accounts able to pre-create paths.
public_references: CWE-59: Improper Link Resolution Before File Access — https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/59.html
